Definition: middle voice from G3144; to be adduced as a witness, i.e. (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation):--take to record, testify.
BiblicalUsage: martýromai is to be adduced as a witness, to testify solemnly, to charge with an oath. In Acts 20:26 Paul takes his hearers to record that he is pure from the blood of all men, and in Acts 26:22 he witnesses to small and great of what the prophets and Moses said should come. In Ephesians 4:17 Paul testifies in the Lord that believers should no longer walk as other Gentiles walk, and in 1 Thessalonians 2:12 he charges them to walk worthy of God. The word is testimony that binds the hearer.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe martýromai teaches me that a witness can also be a solemn charge. I hold that Paul's testimony to the Gentiles is the charge I inherit.
